name: Night One

date.source: The broadcast's own text dates itself "February 28th, 1998"; posted in ten parts to rec.sport.pro-wrestling.fantasy, 1 March 1998.

appearances.note: Shown in a pre-show clip package defeating Dan Kauffman; does not wrestle this broadcast.

matches.note: Hansen retains against his own estranged former partner in a bloody main-event-adjacent match, then attacks him with a chair after the bell.
Requiem and Casey James briefly ally to eliminate Gunnar Gaines, then turn on each other; Tiger Claw runs in to strike Requiem, letting James finish him with the Blackheart Punch for the pinfall.

notes: Card as posted, six further matches not structured for want of a held/minted participant on every side: a UWF elimination-by-submission match (advertised as Fabulous Ones vs. Anarchy, contested in the broadcast itself as Anarchy defending against different opponents); a four-way table dance for the EMWC World Television Championship (Pietro Sandini, "Crimson" Joe Reed, Danny Dynamite, Dirt Dog Unique Allah -- Joe Reed wins the title from Danny Dynamite with a slingshot powerslam through a table); an IEWA Female Fracas (Jessica Starbird vs. the promotion's own Women's TV Champion, Melody -- the served text does not resolve the finish cleanly); an MLWO three-way (Sean Stevens, The Man From Heck, Kevin Legend -- The Man From Heck retains the MLWO North American Championship, then is attacked by Legend after the bell); an MLWO singles match (Captain Midnight vs. Daemon Dempsey, result not read); an MLWO tag match (Matt Harris and Steve Spector defeat Paradox and Tommy Marauder, a bloody hardcore brawl, Harris pinning Paradox); and a SCRA World Championship match (Gangsta Impasse defeats the champion, "Cowboy" Ken Curtis, to win the title). A UWF steel cage match (Serge Annis defeats Bishop) is also collected but not structured; both names collide too heavily with unrelated held characters across the tree to identify safely.

name: Night Two

date.source: The broadcast's own text dates itself "March 1st, 1998"; posted in fifteen parts to rec.sport.pro-wrestling.fantasy, 5 March 1998.

appearances.note: Presents the Deschenes Cup and runner-up plaques; punched by a departing Creed in the parking lot afterward.
Challenges for the EMWC World Heavyweight Championship in a match the served text does not resolve cleanly.

matches.note: Myers wins by pinfall with his own Rattler DDT finisher.
Myers wins with a Hurracanrana, per the broadcast's own closing highlight reel.

matches.stipulation: IIWF Heavyweight Championship of the World, Progressive Death Match

matches.note: Myers wins by small package after both men trade the Cattlebuster DDT and the Rattler; crowned the tournament's first and only champion.
Ronnie wins by escaping the cage, hitting the Ronnieplex on the way down.

notes: The Rich and Infamous (Hayvin Coules and Vince Valor) retain the MLWO World Tag Team Championship in an eight-team tournament final over Kentucky Fried Outlaws; the other three first-round teams (Epitome of Cool, The Benjamins, and the semi-final opponents) are not held or minted, so the bracket itself is not structured. An advertised UWF World Title match (Sebastien Jericho vs. The Reformer) and an advertised Free-For-All "World Invitational Championship" match on both nights' own posted preview cards do not appear in either broadcast's own surviving text.
